teaching: Do not dwell on success, and by this very nondwelling success will not leave: do your work, do your best and keep going; obsess over success (money and fame) and you cannot see clearly, just as trying to be happy is a recipe for misery (Tao Te Ching, Chapter 2, Thomas Cleary translation).
youtube_title: The More You Chase Success, the Less You See

word_overrides.why: 'So, so, so, if all you're focused on is success' x5: each 'so' is a sibilant then a voiced burst (815.12, 815.36/815.40, 815.54/815.64); 'if' is the weak burst at 815.88-815.98, so the hook starts in the dip at 815.84. The five 'success' pairs (soft 'suc', loud 'cess') read off the envelope at 817.48/.70, 817.84/818.02, 818.16/.34, 818.52/.72, 818.90 with its hiss to 819.5; the fifth is very soft (large-v3 on the source hears it, the QA pass and large-v3 on the assembled audio do not), so it stays in the audio and off the captions
medium.en put 'you're' at 819.86 in the cut 'success, success, sorry'; the voice rises at 823.40
medium.en put 'So' at 829.50 in the pause; large-v3 on the stretch alone hears 'So you just do your work' from the rise at 830.64
the 'and' after 'or to others' is soft and comes 1.8 s later (839.66; medium and large-v3 both hear it there), so the pause is cut before it, not after it; large-v3: 'keep going, and, and don't'
large-v3: 'can, like, we'll do our best'; the segment starts after 'like' (dip at 886.36-886.44)
large-v3: 'but we don't, like, become obsessed'; onsets off the envelope
soft 'and' just before 'you're' (QA pass and envelope); medium.en put it in the pause at 827.24
'and' rises at 748.00 just before 'do' (QA pass); medium.en had 747.24 in the tail of 'presumption'
'That's' after 'going' (890.36-890.48), 'all' 890.72; large-v3 and the QA pass both put 'That's' before 890.76
medium.en and large-v3 hear 'I mean' in the one burst at 900.44-900.70 (the QA pass misses it)

phrases: going to be | able to see

image.note: the blind leading the blind into the ditch (pan from the stumbling leader to the fallen): 'you're going to be obsessed, and you're not going to be able to see as clearly' (on the join; covers the second join)
reapers swinging their scythes at the harvest: 'All beings work without exception' (on the join)
the blacksmith and his men at the glowing forge: 'So you just do your work, do your best' (on the join)
a barefoot ascetic striding on along the river: 'and just keep going, don't be preoccupied with this abstract construct' (on the join)
Holbein's rich man at his heaped gold as Death takes it (pan from the miser to Death): 'money brings no peace, and fame even less so. I'm talking about large amounts of money'
a poet fisherman at ease on his raft, line out, whatever the catch: 'We'll do our best. If it works, it works. If it doesn't, it doesn't' (on the join)
Budai, the laughing monk: 'it means peace. It means harmony. It means joy, constant joy'
